blocks.text: Imports Redis and vector clients, loads configuration, and defines slugification. A ContextVar is reserved for the request-local app slug so concurrent tasks do not share an ordinary module global.
blocks.title: Dependencies and request context

blocks.text: The context value wins, with Redis as the fallback for older callers. _namespaced applies the slug except for keys whose identity belongs to a session, workspace, provider account, registry, or shared cache.
blocks.title: Slug lookup and key isolation

blocks.text: The vector index is constructed only when requested, allowing import-time users that only need Redis to run without vector configuration. Missing configuration raises instead of creating a misleading client.
blocks.title: Lazy vector client

blocks.anchor: def write(key: str, value, ex: int = None):
blocks.text: write serializes one value and keeps the local app-slug context synchronized for the special app_slug key. write_many uses one pipeline request and applies one optional expiry to every item.
blocks.title: Single and batched writes

blocks.anchor: def read_stage_output_text(session_id: str, role: str) -> str | None:
blocks.text: This helper reads the stage_output key and accepts either a plain string or a dictionary containing text. Empty and unsupported shapes become None so callers can distinguish missing usable output.
blocks.title: Stage-output normalization

blocks.text: The bulk read preserves original key names while applying namespacing internally. The remaining helpers expose a bare Redis ping, deletion, and atomic integer increments with optional first-write expiry.
blocks.title: Reads, health checks, and counters

blocks.anchor: def _summarize_plan_diff(old_plan: dict | None, new_plan: dict) -> str:
blocks.text: The diff helper compares the plan fields that the planner contract supplies and formats a compact description. It is intentionally separate from persistence so the text can be tested and reused.
blocks.title: Plan change description

blocks.anchor: def write_plan(plan: dict, why: str = None) -> dict:
blocks.text: write_plan appends a timestamped changelog entry before replacing current_plan. It keeps only the configured recent history and returns the plan passed by the caller.
blocks.title: Current plan and history

purpose: This module is the shared key-value boundary for the application. It keeps ordinary keys isolated by the active app slug while leaving session and system keys stable, then centralizes JSON encoding, batching, counters, and plan changelog writes.

Upstash Vector client construction when vector access is first requested
